title: Slipping out at night to hear dance bands
summary: Against his father's wishes he sneaked out to Los Angeles on the red car to hear the Sunnyland Band and possibly King Oliver.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: At what point in your study of music did you decide that you wanted to become a professional musician?
I -- well, that became almost a necessity. That was more or less later on. As I said before,
my father being very, very strict and me being very interested in music, I used to pull some capers that didn't fit with his way of thinking at all.
Well, we used to wait until he went to bed, and then we'd slip out the side window, and I'd go downtown and listen to the dance bands and things. In those days it was very safe. And --
Do you remember what bands you heard in that period?

I used to go all the way over to Los Angeles to hear the Sunnyland Band, which was very popular. And, oh, several -- any band that came through the lower California area, there used to be quite a few of them that would come through, and so I'd slip out and go.
Do you remember specifically any band that you saw?

I think I heard King Oliver one time. And mostly the general -- just the local bands, which, as I say, in those days the bands in person were quite good, many of them quite good, and invariably the next day somebody would come back and tell my father, 'I saw your son last night.' He said, 'I don't see how that can be possible. They were home in bed.' And so that continued and continued for quite a time.
Now, when you and Harold would do that,
you had -- from Pasadena to Los Angeles is how far, about ten miles, 12 miles?
Well, in fact I did it alone. I didn't take Harold. Harold wasn't that interested. And we used to catch the red car -- called the red car down ON Fair Oaks -- and ride over.
You'd take the great big street car.

Yes, big red car. And the dance let out at 1:00 o'clock. So therefore we'd have to leave a little early so we'd catch that last red car going back to Pasadena and slip back in the window and get in bed so no one was the wiser, until it just kept up so long, that my father got suspicious and --
